description: Headless Python script that modifies or filters the NIfTI volumes of a BIDS dataset (e.g. intensity threshold or Gaussian smoothing), optionally guided by a NeuroVue correction patch, and writes the filtered volumes to the session output directory.

bids_dir.description: BIDS dataset whose anatomical volumes are filtered.

correction_patch.description: Optional NeuroVue correction patch that parameterizes the filter.

amount.description: Operation magnitude (FWHM mm for smooth, intensity for threshold).

block.label: Filter Volumes (Python)
block.description: Apply a NIfTI filter operation with a Python script.

requirements: Python 3.10+ with nibabel and numpy (scipy optional, for faster smoothing); set NEUROFLOW_PYTHON to the environment
neuroflow/launch.description: python_tool.mjs checks the Python environment, then calls nf_filter_volumes.run(bids_dir, operation, amount), which writes the filtered volumes to $NEUROFLOW_OUTPUT_DIR/filtered and appends a provenance line.

useWhen: Smooth, threshold or z-score every anatomical volume of a BIDS dataset in one step.

avoidWhen.when: You have loose volumes rather than a BIDS dataset: this tool reads the anatomical volumes from bids_dir.

preconditions: Python 3.10+ with nibabel and numpy (scipy optional, for faster smoothing); NEUROFLOW_PYTHON set to that environment.
bids_dir is a BIDS dataset with anatomical NIfTI volumes.
effects: Writes the filtered volumes to <output dir>/filtered and appends a provenance line; the dataset is not changed.
amount is the FWHM in mm for smooth and an intensity for threshold.

duration.basis: Measured once: 0.1 s on a one-subject gallery dataset; grows with the number and size of volumes.

failures.meaning: No Python environment was found for the tool.
failures.remedy: Set NEUROFLOW_PYTHON to a Python 3.10+ environment that has the packages this tool lists.

failures.meaning: The Python environment lacks a required package.
failures.remedy: The message names the package and the fix: pip install it into that environment, or point NEUROFLOW_PYTHON at one that has it.
